analysis:
This batch contains only changelog fragments and docs/architecture/inference.md. No code is supplied, so I reviewed documented behavior only.

Security-relevant claims:
- Releases register `cluster_runtime` facts (worker, metallib and paged-attention digests, per-model pair-serving grants and parity qualifications), gated per environment by *_CLUSTER_RUNTIME_ENABLED variables. A coordinator that accepts the block then approves two-Mac clusters automatically.
- Declared public models now get grants and qualifications from a checked-in declaration. See the finding on docs/architecture/inference.md ~5275: the qualification scope is wider than its evidence.
- Qwen speculative assistant: it is now excluded from coordinator-paired setups. `ClusterConfiguration.validate` and the leader's pre-stop approval check refuse it. This tightens behavior. It needs checking that the pre-check really precedes stopping parts.
- Heartbeat file split (`service-health.json` vs `part-health.json`) is an availability fix. The supervisor still accepts only a beat with the service's own PID. The new owner-only file path was not checked.
- The pair is now re-offered after an hour when its coordinator-paired parts end quickly. Coordinator-decided registration-timeout ends no longer count toward the three-strike fallback to local API. This is an availability and fallback change. It does not obviously weaken authorization, but the retry logic is not visible.
- The `min_p` change on a single Mac affects sampling only.
- The runtime-facts handling that leaves out another model's catalog ID must not silently drop a model that should be qualified. This needs code review.

No code, coordinator grant enforcement (platform-owned), or signing-lane secrets handling was visible. Further review should cover those once code is supplied.

findings.detail: The updated docs and changelog say GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-27B are declared for public cluster traffic in pipeline and tensor parallel. A coordinator derives their qualifications from a checked-in declaration (`ClusterPublicModels`) and applies them to the whole declared family "on any Apple silicon pair", because "the placement names the evidence, not a limit". The changelog admits that no pipeline ran on two M5 Ultras and that GLM-5.3-Flash has no tensor-parallel cross-cable record, so both rest on the owner's decision. Pair members report only hardware capabilities, so a grant is the only gate on who may serve consumer prompts. A provider (ADV-001) with a different chip or memory class could then serve public traffic under a qualification never exercised on that hardware or mode. That risks wrong outputs or an incorrectly trusted build, which T-054 and T-056 treat as limits of attestation. The threat model does not describe this declaration-derived qualification path or the new `cluster_runtime` release registration. It should record that parity evidence does not cover the applied scope, and name who may change the declaration.
findings.title: Public cluster qualification extended to any Apple silicon pair on owner decision, beyond evidence placement
